transcript:
Meeting header: 2028-11-21 11:00 AM PST | Duration ~75m
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood SRE); Mark (Blue Harbor CTO), Sophie (Blue Harbor SRE), Liam (Blue Harbor ML), Asha (Blue Harbor Product), Eli (Blue Harbor Procurement)

Summary: Quick scoping to align on how Blue Harbor wants TTFT vs TPOT acceptance defined for a 6-week POC. Focus on burstiness/tail-latency impact, sampling plan (steady vs replay vs burst), and clear pass/fail criteria at p95/p99 for both TTFT and TPOT. Action items and next steps captured.

Topics: POC goals, traffic profile and burstiness, TTFT definition and measurement window, TPOT composition (including system-level overhead), p95/p99 targets, cold-start / KV cache warmups, sampling and replay plan, timeline and success criteria.

00:00 Alex: hey everyone thanks for carving time today, I think we have about an hour and 15, we'll try to cover scope and acceptance criteria first.
00:18 Mark: yeah thanks Alex, quick context — Blue Harbor has chat-assist integrations in our research portal. We see lots of spikes when batch jobs finish, so burstiness and tail behavior are our primary concern.
00:32 Sophie: also we have strict p99 goals, like anything beyond 800ms for first token really starts to impact UX for scientists.
00:45 Priya: got it. when you say first token, are you measuring time-to-first-token from request ingress or from user click? small but important difference.
00:52 Sophie: from request ingress — that's where we can instrument.
01:05 Jordan: ok so we'll treat TTFT as ingress->first-byte at the edge, and TPOT as total per-token time which includes generation and network egress. we'll also capture server-side compute time separately.
01:22 Liam: rough numbers — average prompt length 120 tokens, average output 220 tokens, but there are tails where outputs hit 2k tokens. Traffic baseline is 8 rps steady, but bursts up to 180 rps for short windows (30s-2min).
01:40 Samir: that burst profile is, uh, quite spiky. we need to clarify burst shaping during POC — do you want us to inject synthetic bursts or replay real traces?
01:50 Mark: ideally both. replay for fidelity and synthetic to stress upper bounds.
01:56 Alex: excellent. for the POC we'll run two measurement modalities: 1) replay of sanitized traces you provide covering 72 hours to capture real request interarrival distribution; 2) synthetic burst sweeps where we scale qps while holding payload distributions constant to observe degradation curves.
02:18 Asha: and about targets — we mentioned p95 and p99, but we have internal business tiers: "interactive" flows require p95 TTFT < 200ms and p99 < 400ms, while "analysis" flows are okay with p95 TTFT < 500ms and p99 < 800ms. are those achievable?
02:38 Priya: we need model selection and quantization context — which models are you planning to use in production? smaller models will hit those numbers more easily.
02:47 Liam: we currently use an open Llama-derivative for non-sensitive queries and a fine-tuned 33B private model for research. POC should evaluate both if possible.
02:58 Jordan: note that 33B will affect both TTFT and TPOT — especially token time for long sequences. we'll suggest a compatible small variant for fallback in the POC and measure hybrid routing.
03:14 Sophie: also K/V cache warmup matters. bursts cause many cold contexts and KV cache misses on the large model. is your measurement going to distinguish cold vs warmed cache?
03:25 Priya: yes, we'll run controlled warmup runs and tag requests as 'cold' or 'hot'. warmup policy: 10 minutes steady traffic at expected qps before measurement window to populate KV caches, and a separate cold-window with no warmup to measure worst-case.
03:44 Mark: great. what about how you compute TPOT? do you include client-side egress time?
03:51 Alex: for clarity our measurement will emit three metrics: TTFT (ingress->first byte), server_compute_time (first byte->last byte at server), TPOT (total per token as server_compute_time divided by token_count, plus network egress delta if you want an end-user-visible TPOT). we'll provide both server-only and end-to-end numbers.
04:15 Eli: procurement question — do you provide signed time-stamped artifacts so we can include them in the vendor assessment?
04:21 Alex: yes, we'll provide test run artifacts, dashboards, and an artifacts bundle you can store for audit.
04:30 Liam: for p95/p99 targets, can you propose a realistic matrix we should accept? maybe two tiers: interactive and batch/analysis?
04:38 Priya: here's a suggested acceptance matrix — Interactive TTFT p95 < 250ms, p99 < 500ms; Interactive TPOT p95 < 30ms/token, p99 < 70ms/token. Analysis TTFT p95 < 600ms, p99 < 1.2s; Analysis TPOT p95 < 70ms/token, p99 < 150ms/token. These are configurable but based on similar pilots we've run.
05:05 Mark: that's helpful. for Blue Harbor our engineering bar is a little tighter so could we tighten interactive TTFT p95 to 200ms?
05:12 Priya: we can aim for that on small model route, but for the 33B route we may need to show fallback routing or adaptive batching to meet that. tradeoffs will be explicit in the report.
05:28 Jordan: important to call out sampling windows. p99 is sensitive to sample size: we prefer rolling windows of 15 minutes for steady-state and event-window aggregation for bursts. during the burst sweep we recommend 1-minute buckets for high fidelity on the tail.
05:45 Sophie: ok. and what about synthetic concurrency — do you think queueing will inflate TTFT unfairly at the edge?
05:52 Samir: queueing does inflate TTFT; we'll instrument queue length and queue time. If queueing is dominating, we surface it separately and propose autoscale/priority lanes.
06:05 Mark: where does caching of repeated prompts fit in? we have a small set of templated prompts that are likely to be heavily reused.
06:12 Priya: we'll include a cache-hit dimension. we'll run runs with cache enabled and disabled. cache hit ratio will be reported alongside delta on TTFT and TPOT.
06:22 Liam: measurement tooling — will you give us the harness or do we run it?
06:26 Alex: Redwood provides the benchmark harness (github link) and a small self-contained runner. For replay we need sanitized trace in CSV or JSONL. For synthetic bursts we provide a load spec. We'll also run at least two supervised runs in Redwood-managed env and share raw logs.
06:42 Asha: timeline — what are realistic POC milestones?
06:46 Jordan: propose 6 weeks: Week 0 (kickoff & trace handoff), Week 1 (harness delivery + local smoke), Week 2-3 (replay + baseline), Week 4 (burst sweeps and cold-warm comparisons), Week 5 (reporting + remediation recommendations), Week 6 (final acceptance).
07:05 Mark: that works for us but procurement needs cost ballpark for the dedicated infra runs.
07:10 Alex: we'll provide a cost estimate for two supervised runs and a breakdown of compute hours per model variant.
07:15 Eli: for acceptance, do you require both models to pass or is fallback allowed?
07:20 Priya: acceptance can be framed as: primary model path must meet interactive targets for >=95% of steady-state traffic and fallback path must keep degradation within acceptable bounds for tails. we'll make the charter explicit.
07:33 Liam: what about DB callouts during prompt prep? some prompts include live DB enrichment that adds variability. can you simulate that latency?
07:41 Jordan: yes we can add synthetic upstream latency to the harness; we'll run two modes: enriched (extra 50-200ms upstream) and plain.
07:51 Sophie: any security/compliance ask for trace export? we will redact identifiers but keep timing and size.
07:56 Alex: that's fine. we'll provide a redaction checklist.
08:03 Mark: excellent. can you also show a short example of how you'll present failure modes in the report?
08:08 Priya: we'll include waterfall traces, sample slow requests, and a matrix mapping degradation root-causes (queueing, cold K/V miss, model compute) to recommended mitigations.
08:20 Asha: ok final recap please.
08:24 Alex: recap: Redwood will share benchmark harness and runbook by 2028-11-23; Blue Harbor to hand off 72h sanitized traces by 2028-11-28; Redwood to run initial replay+baseline and synthetic burst sweeps weeks of 2028-12-11 and 2028-12-18; deliver interim report week 2028-12-21 and final acceptance artefacts by 2029-01-05. Acceptance criteria: Interactive TTFT p95 target 200-250ms (Blue Harbor will confirm strict threshold), p99 400-500ms; TPOT targets per matrix above. action items in the doc.
08:58 Liam: thanks all, feel good about scope.
09:02 Eli: procurement will follow up on SOW and billing.
09:10 Alex: great, we'll send next steps and calendar invites. thanks everyone.

Notes about transcript quality: speaker overlaps occasional, some product names may be mistranscribed (e.g., "KV cash" vs KV cache), proper nouns sometimes fuzzy.

Referenced artifacts/links: benchmark harness (github.com/redwood/pocharness-sample), sample DASHBOARD link (redwood.app/d/poctemp/bhl-run1), security redaction checklist (redwood.com/docs/redaction-checklist).
